description:
The accounting SPA as a shared deployment of an APP-HOST tenant (AB#5210).

Install this on a root that hosts the app — today `accounting` and `bernkopf`.
One Helm release serves every tenant below it: the app reads the tenant from
its `/:tenantId` route, and `available-tenants.service.ts` walks the root's
descendants to depth 2, skipping any child that has children of its own
(a grouping/identity tenant) in favour of its grandchildren.

Seeds exactly the two entities that make an app host self-contained:

1. `System.Identity/Client` — the OIDC client (authorization code + PKCE, no
   secret) with `AutoProvisionInChildTenants: true`, so every DIRECT child
   gets a mirror instead of an operator adding redirect URIs by hand.
2. `System.Communication/Application` — the Helm deployment (aa0…210), with
   `rootTenantId` bound to the tenant it is installed on.

WHY ONE HOST PER ROOT, NOT ONE FOR THE WHOLE TREE

Client mirroring is deliberately ONE level: `ClientMirrorProvisioningService`
resolves DIRECT children only, and writes each mirror with
`AutoProvisionInChildTenants: false` so it cannot cascade — "a grandchild is
its own parent's business" (AB#5025). A single host on `accounting` would
therefore reach `meshmakers` and `salzburgdev`, but never the four companies
below `bernkopf`. The app could render them; identity would not issue for
them. Hence: `accounting` hosts its own leaves, `bernkopf` hosts its four.

WHY THE CLIENTID IS PER ROOT

`${octo.tenantId}-app`, not a shared name. `bernkopf` is itself a child of
`accounting`, so a shared ClientId made the parent's auto-provision overwrite
the child's own client — the mirror carries the PARENT's redirect URIs, and
sign-in on the child's host died with `invalid redirect_uri`. That happened on
prod-1 on 2026-08-31 and was only noticed on 2026-09-15. Distinct ClientIds
remove the collision by construction; the SPA receives its ClientId through a
ValueOverride anyway.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE

No `Meshmakers.Accounting` CK model dependency: an app host carries no
accounting data. Both production roots hold 0 pipelines, and `bernkopf` is a
pure identity tenant. The Pool (670…001) and Mesh Adapter (670…002) belong to
the service-managed System.Communication blueprint — this seed associates to
the existing Pool rather than fighting the service for ownership.

INSTALL NOTES

`Hostname`, `Values`, `ChartVersion`, `IngressEnabled` and `DeploymentState`
are `isRuntimeState` (AB#4706), so the seeded values apply on a FRESH install
only and a re-apply never overwrites what the operator set. The seeded
hostname is a starting point — set the real public hostname after the first
install. Since System.Identity 2.19.0 the client's URI attributes are
runtime-state too (AB#5210), for exactly the same reason.
